scope: Experimental one-session supervisor runtime/control seam behind LAPIS_BUILD_SUPERVISOR_RUNTIME. This is not persistent process ownership, launchd registration, GUI integration, package update behavior, or production session-service supervision.

implementation.state: Reuses the supervisor state registry and adds explicit blocked-reason stop state.
implementation.runtime: Injected child launcher, ownership record, bounded restart admission, adoption, disable, and lifecycle control.
implementation.control: Private AF_UNIX listener with effective-UID peer check, bounded four-byte length framing, bounded JSON replies, and malformed/oversized connection closure.

verification.name: initial-parent-ctest
verification.result: Caught the worker-masked oversized-frame close defect: supervisor-runtime failed 'an oversized frame closes the client'.

verification.name: control-framing-repair
verification.result: Repaired header/payload state handling so oversized clients close, complete frames process in one poll cycle, payload bytes are appended, and served clients retire.

verification.name: final-parent-ctest
verification.result: 2/2 passed on the socket-capable parent host.

non_claims: No launchd registration, daemon CLI, production client, GUI route, or package update path.
The harmless child fixture proves only the ownership seam, not existing session-service integration.
No real supervisor crash, login/reboot, application replacement, multi-session restore, sanitizer, or static-analysis run.
Adoption remains based on a private ownership record and PID liveness, not a qualified session-service handshake.
